queries_run: ETN Eaton top customer revenue concentration 10-K 2026
Eaton Corporation customer concentration risk disclosure data center hyperscaler
Eaton 10-Q 2025 hyperscaler customer paused slowed data center projects

findings.claim: Eaton FY2024 10-K discloses segment-level customer concentration: 26% of Electrical Americas and Electrical Global segment sales were to eight large electrical products/systems customers; 23% of Aerospace segment sales were to four large aircraft OEMs; 28% of Vehicle segment sales were to two large vehicle OEMs.
findings.source: Eaton Corp plc Form 10-K FY2024 (SEC EDGAR, filed for fiscal year ended 2024-12-31)

findings.claim: In its 2025 Q1/Q2 10-Q filings, Eaton disclosed that one hyperscaler data center customer had paused or slowed some early-stage data center projects while simultaneously making significant investments elsewhere, indicating Eaton actively discloses hyperscaler-specific demand changes as a risk factor.
findings.source: Eaton Corp plc Form 10-Q (Q1 2025, filed 2025-03-31 period) / Form 10-Q (Q2 2025, filed 2025-06-30 period), SEC EDGAR

findings.claim: Despite the one-hyperscaler pause disclosed earlier in 2025, Eaton's Q4 2025 results/commentary showed data center orders surging roughly 200% in the quarter, indicating the broader hyperscaler customer base's spending momentum re-accelerated rather than reflecting sustained credit or demand deterioration across the customer base.
findings.source: Eaton Q4 2025 earnings slides/commentary, via Investing.com coverage "Eaton Q4 2025 slides: Data center surge drives record results as Mobility spin-off announced"

customer_concentration_credit.note: No evidence found of outright credit-rating downgrades, bankruptcy, or balance-sheet stress at any named Eaton top customer (hyperscalers, aircraft OEMs, vehicle OEMs) as of the search date; concentration is disclosed at the segment/customer-count level rather than by named single-customer % of total consolidated revenue.

queries_run: electrical equipment industry shortage transformers switchgear structural oversupply 2026 2027
electrical equipment grid transformer demand outlook 2027 2028 consensus growth forecast
ETN Eaton product demand durability structural 2026

findings.claim: Analysts see multi-year deficits in U.S. transformer supply persisting even as manufacturers invest billions in new capacity; 2026 market demand is projected to beat 2024 levels by 21% for power transformers and 16% for GSUs (generator step-up transformers), and lead times for high-capacity transformers now reach three to four years versus roughly one year in 2020-2021, with high-voltage circuit breakers reaching ~125 weeks.
findings.source: POWER Magazine, "Transformers in 2026: Shortage, Scramble, or Self-Inflicted Crisis?"

findings.claim: The grid-equipment constraint is characterized as structural rather than purely cyclical: data center load growth, grid upgrades, renewable interconnection, industrial electrification, and utility replacement cycles are all competing for the same transformer, switchgear, and breaker manufacturing capacity, with deficits expected to persist through at least 2030.
findings.source: eepower.com / Environment+Energy Leader coverage on grid equipment bottleneck (aggregated from Wood Mackenzie and RMI supply-chain analysis)

findings.claim: Major manufacturers including Hitachi Energy (>$1B including a $457M Virginia plant targeting largest-in-nation capacity by 2028), Siemens Energy ($150M Charlotte NC plant, production start early 2027), and Eaton itself ($340M three-phase transformer facility in South Carolina, targeting a 2027 start) are all adding new large-power-transformer capacity, meaning meaningful new supply begins arriving 2027-2028.
findings.source: POWER Magazine, "Transformers in 2026: Shortage, Scramble, or Self-Inflicted Crisis?"

findings.claim: Global power transformer market is estimated at $28.2B in 2026, forecast to reach $46.4B by 2033 (7.4% CAGR); data center electricity consumption (about 4.4% of U.S. electricity in 2023) is projected to double or triple by 2028, and in April 2026 the U.S. invoked the Defense Production Act to boost domestic transformer/substation/high-voltage component manufacturing, with DOE allocating $375M in January 2026 to strengthen the transformer supply chain.
findings.source: Future Market Insights transformer market report; IEA "Building the Future Transmission Grid" supply-chain report

supply_demand_durability.note: Evidence points to a durable, multi-year (through ~2030) structural supply deficit for grid electrical equipment rather than a purely cyclical spike, but new capacity (including Eaton's own $340M SC facility) starts landing 2027-2028, which is a forward risk to pricing/lead-time tailwinds that should be flagged as a monitorable trigger rather than assumed away.
